summary: Sunday run with no newer arXiv announcement block than Friday, 24 July 2026. Selected papers emphasize transverse-spherocity interpretation, hydrodynamic v02(pT) predictions, misspecification-aware likelihood inference, neural residual solvers for QCD functional equations, uncertainty-aware plasma surrogates, and Bayesian evidence search for neutron-source mixtures.
strongest_paper: 2607.21161: Intrinsic coupling between transverse spherocity and elliptic flow in heavy-ion collisions
top_takeaway: The most consequential heavy-ion result is the warning that spherocity-selected heavy-ion samples may primarily encode elliptic-flow anisotropy rather than jet-like topology; the most broadly useful AI/statistics result is the well-tempered likelihood for misspecified physics models.

papers.title: Intrinsic coupling between transverse spherocity and elliptic flow in heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract: The paper argues, using toy Monte Carlo, AMPT, and analytic reasoning, that transverse spherocity in heavy-ion collisions is intrinsically related to elliptic flow and should be interpreted primarily as collective momentum anisotropy rather than jetty topology.

papers.title: Enhanced hydrodynamic predictions for v02(pT)
papers.authors: Rupam Samanta, Tribhuban Parida, Jean-Yves Ollitrault
papers.abstract: The paper presents hydrodynamic predictions for v02(pT), including charged and identified hadron behavior in Pb+Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV, after applying a data-driven correction to match v2(pT) data.

papers.title: The Well-Tempered Likelihood: Honest Confidence Intervals for Misspecified Models
papers.abstract: The paper proposes dividing likelihood-ratio test statistics by a goodness-of-fit statistic so confidence intervals self-limit under model misspecification, including an unbinned classifier two-sample-test formulation.

papers.title: Neural solutions of coupled ghost and gluon Dyson-Schwinger equations in Landau gauge
papers.abstract: A neural residual representation solves coupled ghost and gluon DSEs, agreeing with fixed-point solutions at the percent level while showing neural error below truncation-model uncertainty.

papers.title: Cycle-Consistent and Uncertainty-Aware Neural Surrogates for Tokamak Edge Plasmas
papers.authors: Abdourahmane Diaw, Sebastian De Pascuale, Jae-Sun Park, Ivan Paradela Perez, Jeremy D. Lore, Stefan Dasbach
papers.abstract: The paper builds fast conditional U-Net and ensemble surrogates for tokamak edge plasmas with cycle-consistent inverse recovery and uncertainty estimates.

papers.title: Bayesian evidence adaptive pursuit to identify neutron sources with scatter-based spectrometers
papers.authors: David Breitenmoser, William Heriot, Peter Marleau, Shaun D. Clarke, Sara A. Pozzi
papers.abstract: The paper presents a scalable Bayesian evidence search for neutron source mixtures, validated with controlled neutron measurements and high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations.

papers.title: Searching for initial state fluctuations in heavy ion collisions at FAIR energy using Principal Component Analysis
papers.abstract: The paper introduces hot-spot-like initial-state fluctuations in UrQMD Pb+Pb events at FAIR energy and studies PCA eigenvalues of pion final-state distributions.

papers.title: Impact of Baryon anti-Baryon annihilation on hyperon production and apparent strangeness enhancement in anti-Lambda/anti-proton at SPS energy
papers.abstract: The paper uses UrQMD to argue that baryon-antibaryon annihilation can explain features of anti-Lambda/anti-proton enhancement, cautioning against a simple strangeness-enhancement interpretation.
